---

# Report Card

> Building a unit of anything emits its report card. The card is not documentation
> bolted on after — it is the durable artifact the work is born with, the SEED the
> work spawns from, and the honest, graded, two-way-linked account of what the unit
> does and which of its innards do it. A unit shipped without its card is incomplete.

Domain-agnostic. The skin changes (Gherkin for code, circuit-block Given/When/Then
for electronics, request/response for an API); the skeleton never does.

**This skill ships working machinery, not just doctrine.** If a repo has no card
system, install it — don't hand-write prose that evaporates with the conversation.

---

## DO THIS FIRST — is the machinery present?

```bash
ls features/*.feature 2>/dev/null | head -3   # cards exist?
git config core.hooksPath                     # should print .githooks
```

**No cards / no hooks → install, then card.** One command, idempotent, never commits:

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh            # current repo, features/
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh --target /path/to/repo \
    --cards-dir features --title "Foo — Feature Reference"
```

It drops into the repo:

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `features/print-card.py` | cards → `README.md` + printable `dist/` |
| `features/gen-status.py` | cards → `STATUS.md` (the derived test matrix) |
| `features/gen-sessions.py` | Codex transcripts → `SESSIONS.generated.md` |
| `features/cards.conf` | per-repo knobs (title, source extensions, exclusions) |
| `features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt` | the house-style skeleton to copy |
| `features/INDEX.md` | the commit ⇄ card map (the one hand-kept file) |
| `.githooks/pre-commit` + `post-merge` + `report-card-stamp.sh` | the stamp engine |
| `.githooks/pre-commit.local` | repo-local jobs — **yours, never clobbered on reinstall** |
| `core.hooksPath = .githooks` | set for this clone (git won't auto-run committed hooks) |

Then, **every commit onward, with zero effort:** a diff touching a card's `# WATCH:`
symbols stamps a dated RESULT-LOG line into that card *in the same commit*, and a
staged card regenerates `STATUS.md` / `README.md` / `SESSIONS.generated.md` and stages
them too. Mapping is **by symbol, not filename** — touching an unrelated part of a
shared file does not tag every card.

Already installed elsewhere and want the engine refreshed? Re-run `install.sh`; it
overwrites the canonical hooks + generators and keeps `pre-commit.local`, `cards.conf`,
`INDEX.md`, and every card. `--force` to overwrite those too.

## Then: write the card (the same motion as the build)

1. `cp features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt features/<name>.feature` and fill it in.
2. Write `features/<name>.session.md` — the spawning conversation, faithful not
   flattering, with the mandatory **How to get back** block.
3. Back-link the innards: `// REPORT-CARD >> features/<name>.feature` (comment syntax
   of that language).
4. Set the card's `# WATCH:` line to the symbols it owns — that's the hook contract.
5. Enrol it in `features/INDEX.md`.
6. `python3 features/print-card.py --readme` (and `--all` for printable `dist/`).
7. Commit. The hooks do the rest.

**House style, grade ladder, banned anti-patterns:** `reference/house-style.md`.
**Why the format is shaped this way:** `reference/wiki-pattern.md`.

## Just report back to me (works WITHOUT git)

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/report.sh --target ~/work/foo
```

Regenerates every derived view and prints an honest summary: card count, scenario
count, grades in use, and the three failure modes that otherwise stay silent —
cards with **no `# WATCH:` line** (the hooks can never stamp them), cards whose
grade is written as a **trailing comment** instead of a Gherkin tag (no generator
counts it, so they show as ungraded), and cards with **no `.session.md`** (broken
triad). Finds the card home automatically (`features/`, `cards/`, `docs/cards`).

**Git is optional.** Cards, generators and all derived views work on a plain
folder — `install.sh` detects a non-git target, installs everything except the
hooks, and says so. Only RESULT-LOG *stamping* needs git, because it has to know
which symbols a diff touched. In a non-git folder you run `report.sh` yourself
instead of a commit doing it for you.

## cards.conf keys

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `title` | heading of the generated reference |
| `readme_file` | target for `--readme` (default `README.md`) — **set this if `features/README.md` is hand-written**, or it gets clobbered |
| `source_ext` | extensions recognised as "innards" in a `# cite:` line |
| `meta_prefix` | card-name prefixes grouped as meta/process cards |
| `exclude` | cards kept out of `STATUS.md` (rollups, host-side tooling) |
| `readme_exclude` | cards hidden from the reference entirely (rare) |
| `grade_map` | translate a repo's OWN grade words into canonical tiers, e.g. `@untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @built:@code-verified` — the project keeps its vocabulary AND gets a correct matrix |
| `runtime_label` / `hardware_label` / `status_note` | STATUS.md column labels + note |
| `sessions_file` | session-registry filename (default `SESSIONS.generated.md`) |
| `project_dirs` | extra paths whose Codex transcripts belong to this repo |

## Card dialects — indented banners are legal

Some repos put the banner **inside** the `Feature:` block, indented (Paketti does).
The stamp engine matches `# WATCH:` / `RESULT-LOG >>` at **line start with leading
whitespace allowed**, so both dialects stamp, and the inserted line copies the
marker's own indentation. What is still rejected is a *mid-sentence* mention of the
marker in prose, so a card describing the convention can't opt itself in.

A strict column-0 anchor is what made every Paketti card a silent no-op for months —
hooks installed, running, stamping nothing, no error. If cards aren't being stamped,
run `report.sh` before assuming the hooks are broken.

## Verification commands

```bash
python3 features/print-card.py --readme     # regenerate the feature reference
python3 features/print-card.py --all        # per-card dist/ (pure Gherkin + printable)
python3 features/gen-status.py              # regenerate the test matrix
python3 features/gen-sessions.py            # regenerate the session registry
rtfc features/dist/<name>.card.md           # printable card → RTF clipboard
```

All are dependency-free Apple-native python3, deterministic (no timestamps embedded,
so no commit churn), and resolve the card home from `--cards-dir` → `$REPORT_CARDS_DIR`
→ the script's own directory.

---

## The four properties (every card, every domain)

1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result.
   `Given <state>, When <action>, Then <measurable outcome>`.
2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it
   (proc + line + commit; component refdes + node; file + function).
3. **Honestly graded** — one tag per claim. The grade is the anti-lying mechanism.
   `@designed` `@built` `@build-verified` `@sim-verified` `@runtime-verified`
   `@hw-verified` `@untested` `@hw-untested` `@todo` `@stock`.
   Untested is untested. **Never grade up to look finished.**
4. **Two-way** — the innards carry a greppable back-link to the card, so the wiki is
   bidirectional.

## The triad — three legs, all cross-linked

- **`<name>.feature` (the card)** — the spec: graded verifiable claims, each cited to
  its innards. The *what* + *why-as-grade*.
- **`<name>.session.md`** — the spawning conversation stored beside the card: the
  requests, refinements, corrections, rejected options, the "no I didn't do it"
  admissions. **Faithful, not flattering** — the grade's audit trail. This enables the
  **vibe diff**: across versions you diff the code, the card, AND the dialogue that
  drove each change. A card without its session can spawn the code but not the vibe —
  INCOMPLETE.
  **MANDATORY "How to get back" block** — transcript `file://` path, session ID,
  `Codex --resume <id>`, real date+timestamps pulled from the transcript (never
  fabricated; if unconfirmable, say so). `gen-sessions.py` discovers these repo-wide.
  **MANDATORY bundle, don't just link** — a `file://` link rots the moment the
  `.jsonl` moves. Copy the raw transcript beside the card as
  `<name>.transcript.jsonl` (lossless) plus a readable `<name>.transcript.md`. The
  curated `.session.md` is the audit; the bundled transcript is the source.
- **RESULT block** (card header) — what actually shipped: feature commit(s), the PR if
  any ("direct-push, no PR" when none), card-authoring commit(s), files changed.
  Verify delivery by first-parent ancestry — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers
  across forks. The hooks maintain the running RESULT-LOG under it.

Three legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is rebuildable straight from git: load one card →
spec + rationale + diff, no re-reading raw source.

## The card is a generative seed (it comes first)

The card opens with a **WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS** preamble because it spawns three spaces:

- **Codespace** = the file structure — the card's own files plus the innards layout it
  cites. From the card you can scaffold or re-derive the code.
- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning — held in the `.session` (wrong turns included). Also
  what the vibe diff diffs.
- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and must NOT touch, so
  re-spawning stays in-bounds. Make it verifiable with a `@stock` "must not break"
  scenario.

`card ⇒ codespace + areaspace`; `session ⇒ thinkspace`.

## Tests → Features → automatic index (never hand-typed)

The whole point is that **code conveys its own verified status** — a behaviour is
written ONCE and every status view derives from it:

1. **Tests ARE the Features.** A verifiable claim lives once as a graded `Scenario`;
   its `@grade` tags **are** its test status.
2. **Features become the index.** The status view is GENERATED from those tags, run
   automatically by the pre-commit hook, committed alongside the card.
3. **So anyone can confirm** with zero manual labour: tested or not, at what level, and
   where it links (card → innards → commits → session).

**Banned anti-pattern:** hand-maintaining a parallel "what's tested" list. If you catch
yourself typing `runtime-verified` into an index, stop — change the card's tag and let
the index regenerate. A derived view cannot disagree with its source; a hand-kept one
drifts and lies. Generated files carry a `DO NOT EDIT — generated` header.

## Relationship to Convey (`~/work/convey`)

**This skill is the DOCTRINE + SKIN SYSTEM + portable tooling. Convey is the larger
ENGINE.** A report card IS a Convey "Underlying Principle" — a `principles/NNNN-slug/`
folder bound to git. The hooks shipped here are Convey's canonical stamp engine, which
is why `install.sh` and `convey hooks install --target .` are interchangeable for the
hook half.

Mapping (full detail in `~/work/convey/docs/DOCTRINE.md`):

- **Emit a card** = `convey new "<title>" --target <folder> --skin <code|circuit|api|media>`.
- **`.feature`** = stage 1 *Describe*; `convey verify` reconciles the declared grade
  with the actual run and **flags optimism** (OPTIMISTIC / UNVERIFIED) — the anti-lying
  mechanism, automated. Where no runner exists it reports UNRUN and keeps the declared
  grade (never fakes a pass).
- **`.session`** = stage 2 *Sessions* + `convey bundle` copies the lossless transcript
  beside the card and fills "How to get back".
- **RESULT** = stage 3 *Done* (git-derived) + stage 5 *Change*.
- **Two-way back-link** = `convey backlink`. **The wiki** = `convey atlas`.

Use Convey where it's installed; use `scripts/install.sh` for any repo (or machine)
where it isn't. The four properties and three legs are identical either way.

## The card is conversable

The `.feature` is compact distilled text with the bundled session as lossless backing,
so you can hand it to a `file-to-text` → LLM reader and *talk to it*:

```bash
card converse <name>           # resolve by name + fm-converse it (Apple on-device LLM)
card converse <name> --full    # converse over the full bundled transcript
card bundle <name>             # copy + render the spawning session beside the card
card list | show | path        # browse cards
```

`card` lives at `~/work/apple/bin/card`. This is *why* the full session must be
bundled, not merely linked — an `fm-converse` session can't follow a dead `file://`
link, but it can read a sibling file.

**The universality corollary.** The card is the *same skeleton for every file format*,
so the underlying principle of ANY file can be read INTO a card: take a `.lua` tool, a
`.mp4`, a `.sch`, a `.pdf`, a `.wav` — distill what it *does* and *why* into graded
Given/When/Then claims cited to its innards, bundle the session that produced it, and
the card becomes the universal, conversable lens on that file.

## Domain skins (same skeleton)

- **Code** — Gherkin `.feature`; scenarios cite `FILE.ext Proc (~line)` + commit; tags
  for status; back-link comment in the source.
- **Electronics / circuits** — one card per block. `Given Vin = 5.0V, When EN goes
  high, Then Vout settles to 3.3V ±2% within 200µs`; cite parts (`U1 AP2112`, divider
  `R3/R4`, `Cout C7`); grade `@sim-verified @hw-untested`. A whole circuit "already
  contains its report card" = each block ships its card; building the circuit is
  composing cards; the top card is the sum of sub-cards; schematic ⇄ card back-link.
  Pairs with `circuitjs1` / `schematic-to-circuitjs`.
- **API / pipeline / signal chain** — claim = request→response / input→artifact /
  source→processed; cite the endpoint/stage/device; grade by where it's verified.

## Backfilling click-back into an existing session file (retrofit)

When a card/session predates the click-back requirement, identify the spawning
transcript by **content, never by guess**:

1. `cd ~/.Codex/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` (one `.jsonl` per session), or just run
   `gen-sessions.py` which does the discovery repo-wide.
2. Count fixed-string hits per transcript on distinctive strings from the work:
   `for f in *.jsonl; do echo "$(grep -cF -e "PTN0003" -e "Lackluster" "$f")  $f"; done`
   Use `grep -F` / `rg -F` — **never** a regex with `.*` between literals
   (catastrophic-backtracking ban). Confirm with a second distinct probe (65 vs 11 hits
   is decisive; 7 vs 6 is not).
3. Pull the window: first/last `"timestamp"`; convert UTC → local.
4. Add the **How to get back** block, including an "identified by content, not guessed"
   note with the hit count and a "Backfilled: <date>" line.
5. **Honesty:** never fabricate a session ID. If nothing decisively matches, say so.

## The one honest caveat

For domains with no test runner (16-bit TASM assembly, a bench circuit before hardware
exists), the card's claims are *verifiable-in-principle* — a disciplined human/LLM
checklist and session command until automation glue exists. The wiki value (persistent,
compounding, faithful, loadable-as-command, git-rebuildable) holds on day one
regardless of whether the automation is ever written.

---

Global rule: `~/.Codex/AGENTS.md` § "BUILDING ANY UNIT EMITS ITS REPORT CARD".
Reference instance (94 cards, full triads, live hooks): `esaruoho/impulse-tracker`
`features/` — the repo this machinery was isolated from.

5. Enrol it in `features/INDEX.md`.
6. `python3 features/print-card.py --readme` (and `--all` for printable `dist/`).
7. Commit. The hooks do the rest.

**House style, grade ladder, banned anti-patterns:** `reference/house-style.md`.
**Why the format is shaped this way:** `reference/wiki-pattern.md`.

## Just report back to me (works WITHOUT git)

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/report.sh --target ~/work/foo
```

Regenerates every derived view and prints an honest summary: card count, scenario
count, grades in use, and the three failure modes that otherwise stay silent —
cards with **no `# WATCH:` line** (the hooks can never stamp them), cards whose
grade is written as a **trailing comment** instead of a Gherkin tag (no generator
counts it, so they show as ungraded), and cards with **no `.session.md`** (broken
triad). Finds the card home automatically (`features/`, `cards/`, `docs/cards`).

**Git is optional.** Cards, generators and all derived views work on a plain
folder — `install.sh` detects a non-git target, installs everything except the
hooks, and says so. Only RESULT-LOG *stamping* needs git, because it has to know
which symbols a diff touched. In a non-git folder you run `report.sh` yourself
instead of a commit doing it for you.

## cards.conf keys

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `title` | heading of the generated reference |
| `readme_file` | target for `--readme` (default `README.md`) — **set this if `features/README.md` is hand-written**, or it gets clobbered |
| `source_ext` | extensions recognised as "innards" in a `# cite:` line |
| `meta_prefix` | card-name prefixes grouped as meta/process cards |
| `exclude` | cards kept out of `STATUS.md` (rollups, host-side tooling) |
| `readme_exclude` | cards hidden from the reference entirely (rare) |
| `grade_map` | translate a repo's OWN grade words into canonical tiers, e.g. `@untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @built:@code-verified` — the project keeps its vocabulary AND gets a correct matrix |
| `runtime_label` / `hardware_label` / `status_note` | STATUS.md column labels + note |
| `sessions_file` | session-registry filename (default `SESSIONS.generated.md`) |
| `project_dirs` | extra paths whose Codex transcripts belong to this repo |

## Card dialects — indented banners are legal

Some repos put the banner **inside** the `Feature:` block, indented (Paketti does).
The stamp engine matches `# WATCH:` / `RESULT-LOG >>` at **line start with leading
whitespace allowed**, so both dialects stamp, and the inserted line copies the
marker's own indentation. What is still rejected is a *mid-sentence* mention of the
marker in prose, so a card describing the convention can't opt itself in.

A strict column-0 anchor is what made every Paketti card a silent no-op for months —
hooks installed, running, stamping nothing, no error. If cards aren't being stamped,
run `report.sh` before assuming the hooks are broken.

## Verification commands

```bash
python3 features/print-card.py --readme     # regenerate the feature reference
python3 features/print-card.py --all        # per-card dist/ (pure Gherkin + printable)
python3 features/gen-status.py              # regenerate the test matrix
python3 features/gen-sessions.py            # regenerate the session registry
rtfc features/dist/<name>.card.md           # printable card → RTF clipboard
```

All are dependency-free Apple-native python3, deterministic (no timestamps embedded,
so no commit churn), and resolve the card home from `--cards-dir` → `$REPORT_CARDS_DIR`
→ the script's own directory.

---

## The four properties (every card, every domain)

1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result.
   `Given <state>, When <action>, Then <measurable outcome>`.
2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it
   (proc + line + commit; component refdes + node; file + function).
3. **Honestly graded** — one tag per claim. The grade is the anti-lying mechanism.
   `@designed` `@built` `@build-verified` `@sim-verified` `@runtime-verified`
   `@hw-verified` `@untested` `@hw-untested` `@todo` `@stock`.
   Untested is untested. **Never grade up to look finished.**
4. **Two-way** — the innards carry a greppable back-link to the card, so the wiki is
   bidirectional.

## The triad — three legs, all cross-linked

- **`<name>.feature` (the card)** — the spec: graded verifiable claims, each cited to
  its innards. The *what* + *why-as-grade*.
- **`<name>.session.md`** — the spawning conversation stored beside the card: the
  requests, refinements, corrections, rejected options, the "no I didn't do it"
  admissions. **Faithful, not flattering** — the grade's audit trail. This enables the
  **vibe diff**: across versions you diff the code, the card, AND the dialogue that
  drove each change. A card without its session can spawn the code but not the vibe —
  INCOMPLETE.
  **MANDATORY "How to get back" block** — transcript `file://` path, session ID,
  `Codex --resume <id>`, real date+timestamps pulled from the transcript (never
  fabricated; if unconfirmable, say so). `gen-sessions.py` discovers these repo-wide.
  **MANDATORY bundle, don't just link** — a `file://` link rots the moment the
  `.jsonl` moves. Copy the raw transcript beside the card as
  `<name>.transcript.jsonl` (lossless) plus a readable `<name>.transcript.md`. The
  curated `.session.md` is the audit; the bundled transcript is the source.
- **RESULT block** (card header) — what actually shipped: feature commit(s), the PR if
  any ("direct-push, no PR" when none), card-authoring commit(s), files changed.
  Verify delivery by first-parent ancestry — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers
  across forks. The hooks maintain the running RESULT-LOG under it.

Three legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is rebuildable straight from git: load one card →
spec + rationale + diff, no re-reading raw source.

## The card is a generative seed (it comes first)

The card opens with a **WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS** preamble because it spawns three spaces:

- **Codespace** = the file structure — the card's own files plus the innards layout it
  cites. From the card you can scaffold or re-derive the code.
- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning — held in the `.session` (wrong turns included). Also
  what the vibe diff diffs.
- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and must NOT touch, so
  re-spawning stays in-bounds. Make it verifiable with a `@stock` "must not break"
  scenario.

`card ⇒ codespace + areaspace`; `session ⇒ thinkspace`.

## Tests → Features → automatic index (never hand-typed)

The whole point is that **code conveys its own verified status** — a behaviour is
written ONCE and every status view derives from it:

1. **Tests ARE the Features.** A verifiable claim lives once as a graded `Scenario`;
   its `@grade` tags **are** its test status.
2. **Features become the index.** The status view is GENERATED from those tags, run
   automatically by the pre-commit hook, committed alongside the card.
3. **So anyone can confirm** with zero manual labour: tested or not, at what level, and
   where it links (card → innards → commits → session).

**Banned anti-pattern:** hand-maintaining a parallel "what's tested" list. If you catch
yourself typing `runtime-verified` into an index, stop — change the card's tag and let
the index regenerate. A derived view cannot disagree with its source; a hand-kept one
drifts and lies. Generated files carry a `DO NOT EDIT — generated` header.

## Relationship to Convey (`~/work/convey`)

**This skill is the DOCTRINE + SKIN SYSTEM + portable tooling. Convey is the larger
ENGINE.** A report card IS a Convey "Underlying Principle" — a `principles/NNNN-slug/`
folder bound to git. The hooks shipped here are Convey's canonical stamp engine, which
is why `install.sh` and `convey hooks install --target .` are interchangeable for the
hook half.

Mapping (full detail in `~/work/convey/docs/DOCTRINE.md`):

- **Emit a card** = `convey new "<title>" --target <folder> --skin <code|circuit|api|media>`.
- **`.feature`** = stage 1 *Describe*; `convey verify` reconciles the declared grade
  with the actual run and **flags optimism** (OPTIMISTIC / UNVERIFIED) — the anti-lying
  mechanism, automated. Where no runner exists it reports UNRUN and keeps the declared
  grade (never fakes a pass).
- **`.session`** = stage 2 *Sessions* + `convey bundle` copies the lossless transcript
  beside the card and fills "How to get back".
- **RESULT** = stage 3 *Done* (git-derived) + stage 5 *Change*.
- **Two-way back-link** = `convey backlink`. **The wiki** = `convey atlas`.

Use Convey where it's installed; use `scripts/install.sh` for any repo (or machine)
where it isn't. The four properties and three legs are identical either way.

## The card is conversable

The `.feature` is compact distilled text with the bundled session as lossless backing,
so you can hand it to a `file-to-text` → LLM reader and *talk to it*:

```bash
card converse <name>           # resolve by name + fm-converse it (Apple on-device LLM)
card converse <name> --full    # converse over the full bundled transcript
card bundle <name>             # copy + render the spawning session beside the card
card list | show | path        # browse cards
```

`card` lives at `~/work/apple/bin/card`. This is *why* the full session must be
bundled, not merely linked — an `fm-converse` session can't follow a dead `file://`
link, but it can read a sibling file.

**The universality corollary.** The card is the *same skeleton for every file format*,
so the underlying principle of ANY file can be read INTO a card: take a `.lua` tool, a
`.mp4`, a `.sch`, a `.pdf`, a `.wav` — distill what it *does* and *why* into graded
Given/When/Then claims cited to its innards, bundle the session that produced it, and
the card becomes the universal, conversable lens on that file.

## Domain skins (same skeleton)

- **Code** — Gherkin `.feature`; scenarios cite `FILE.ext Proc (~line)` + commit; tags
  for status; back-link comment in the source.
- **Electronics / circuits** — one card per block. `Given Vin = 5.0V, When EN goes
  high, Then Vout settles to 3.3V ±2% within 200µs`; cite parts (`U1 AP2112`, divider
  `R3/R4`, `Cout C7`); grade `@sim-verified @hw-untested`. A whole circuit "already
  contains its report card" = each block ships its card; building the circuit is
  composing cards; the top card is the sum of sub-cards; schematic ⇄ card back-link.
  Pairs with `circuitjs1` / `schematic-to-circuitjs`.
- **API / pipeline / signal chain** — claim = request→response / input→artifact /
  source→processed; cite the endpoint/stage/device; grade by where it's verified.

## Backfilling click-back into an existing session file (retrofit)

When a card/session predates the click-back requirement, identify the spawning
transcript by **content, never by guess**:

1. `cd ~/.Codex/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` (one `.jsonl` per session), or just run
   `gen-sessions.py` which does the discovery repo-wide.
2. Count fixed-string hits per transcript on distinctive strings from the work:
   `for f in *.jsonl; do echo "$(grep -cF -e "PTN0003" -e "Lackluster" "$f")  $f"; done`
   Use `grep -F` / `rg -F` — **never** a regex with `.*` between literals
   (catastrophic-backtracking ban). Confirm with a second distinct probe (65 vs 11 hits
   is decisive; 7 vs 6 is not).
3. Pull the window: first/last `"timestamp"`; convert UTC → local.
4. Add the **How to get back** block, including an "identified by content, not guessed"
   note with the hit count and a "Backfilled: <date>" line.
5. **Honesty:** never fabricate a session ID. If nothing decisively matches, say so.

## The one honest caveat

For domains with no test runner (16-bit TASM assembly, a bench circuit before hardware
exists), the card's claims are *verifiable-in-principle* — a disciplined human/LLM
checklist and session command until automation glue exists. The wiki value (persistent,
compounding, faithful, loadable-as-command, git-rebuildable) holds on day one
regardless of whether the automation is ever written.

---

Global rule: `~/.Codex/AGENTS.md` § "BUILDING ANY UNIT EMITS ITS REPORT CARD".
Reference instance (94 cards, full triads, live hooks): `esaruoho/impulse-tracker`
`features/` — the repo this machinery was isolated from.
"}

## decisions

- Pattern Sync recording must never repurpose an instrument whose MIDI output port and channel are configured: it selects the first empty following slot, or appends an instrument when none is empty.

- The GlobalGainer dialog will use the same value setter as the existing MIDI mappings, with an explicit start/end-chain selector so missing gainers are created consistently.

- TX16W Typhoon/Cyclone item identity uses an observed creator signature, not arbitrary bytes: known-good Cyclone images share `b4 a8 f8 28 a8 c6 d1 86` as the first 8 bytes of every `VInf` stamp, and Paketti exports now keep that signature with ordered Typhoon-like item ids.
- Launch App filter commands require an output route: `$outfile` in the arguments or enabled stdout capture. The runner must preserve the command exit code and stderr so a failed CLI program is reported instead of being indistinguishable from a missing output WAV.
- Renoise exposes Active / Bypassed as a selected automation parameter but not in `AudioDevice.parameters`; Device Control graphical recording verifies the target with numeric `selected_track_device_index`, never userdata equality, rather than falling back to parameter 1 (Mix).

- Ableton FileRef is resolved through RelativePathType, not the absolute Path: 1 means
  relative to the preset file, 5 a Live Pack, 6 the User Library, 7 Live's own resources,
  and every audio reference is Type="2". Writing the wrong root makes Live open the preset
  with its structure intact and every sample marked Missing, which is how it first failed.
- Paketti writes gzip using DEFLATE "stored" blocks. Every conforming reader must accept
  them, so Paketti needs a decompressor but never a compressor — the largest piece of the
  work disappears and the output is still byte-for-byte legal gzip.
- Renoise decodes and encodes the audio, so porting a container format is container and
  metadata only. That is the structural advantage over a standalone converter, which has
  to carry its own codecs.

- Music Mouse F1-F4 treatment shortcuts should only react to bare function keys; modified function keys belong to Renoise/macOS/global shortcuts unless explicitly mapped by Music Mouse.
- Music Mouse Sync overrides Tempo 1 and Tempo 2; the UI should disable ignored free-run controls and expose the effective arpeggio rate so users can see whether playback is synced to Renoise lines or free-running.
- Music Mouse Single note should filter every live and write treatment, including Chord, Arpeggiate, Line, Strum, Improvise, arpeggio stamping, and Record to Row, so hidden grid voices are not still audible or written.
- Music Mouse Sync can only phase-lock when Renoise transport is playing; when stopped it should say it is free-running at the song line duration, because there is no moving playhead line to lock against.
- Music Mouse Arpeggiate and Line should use explicit musical note rates; at LPB 4, 1/16 means one Renoise row, 1/8 means every two rows, 1/32 means two hits per row.
- Music Mouse tempo status should be short enough not to widen the dialog; rate selection needs its own visible row instead of being hidden in the Treatment row.
- Phrase-backed Music Mouse arpeggiation is an opt-in Paketti prototype: it owns a reusable `Paketti Music Mouse Live Arp` phrase, rewrites its notes and length from the current grid, and triggers it through a reserved low phrase-keymap note so Renoise provides the playback clock.
- The Phrase Arp checkbox must remain enabled because enabling it is what switches Music Mouse into Arpeggiate mode and resolves the Strum conflict.
- Phrase-backed playback should support both Arpeggiate and Line; Line keeps its ascending sequence while Arpeggiate retains its selected direction.
- Phrase playback must not rewrite the phrase from its timer callback; Scatter order changes only when its source state changes, so Renoise can provide a stable phrase clock.
- Closing, reloading, or re-opening Music Mouse in Chord mode must restore phrase playback so an old Paketti phrase cannot leak into normal notes.
- Startup cleanup must send note-off to the reserved Paketti phrase trigger before changing the instrument phrase mode.
- Startup cleanup must remove only the mapping attached to Paketti's owned live-arpeggio phrase, so Chord mode cannot retrigger it.
- Chord mode must set the instrument phrase playback mode to `PHRASES_OFF`; Selective mode is still capable of launching phrases.
- Phrase Strum should encode `strum_ms` as phrase delay-column offsets while keeping the phrase loop interval musical and rate-controlled.
- Changing Strum spacing must immediately rewrite an active Phrase Arp phrase.
- Freeze mode must block phrase re-strikes, and arpeggio direction must offer ascending/descending ping-pong cycles.
- The Pattern drag-bar editor should have its own persisted hide flag, independent from Hide Details, so users can keep the controls visible while hiding only the contour editor.
- Music Mouse should treat a selected non-Music-Mouse sample as protected: sound keys warn instead of regenerating or retriggering it, and active contour playback should adopt mouse-position changes on the clock instead of adding immediate off-grid strikes.
- Music Mouse transpose shortcuts must update both the audible notes and the visual readout/canvas; on ISO/Finnish layouts Shift-< should be treated as the upward transpose gesture even if Renoise reports the key name as `<`.
- Music Mouse transpose shortcuts should update the grid state silently when Music Mouse is frozen, keyjazzing, sound-disabled, or mouse-muted; they must not re-trigger the cursor chord from a muted mode.
- Music Mouse Plink should keep its fast percussive decay character but use a longer generated strike, so it reads as a short pitched system sound instead of a pitchless thud.
- Music Mouse Record-to-Pattern stays on right Shift; standalone left Shift must not trigger playback and must leave Shift combos like Shift-< usable. The standalone trigger-this-grid-entry gesture moves from left Shift to standalone Option/Alt.
- Music Mouse `interval` means transpose step size for z/x/<, not a live pattern-playback interval; the UI should name it accordingly.
- Music Mouse Strike controls are sound-design/render controls, not performance gestures: Plink/Bell/Gong, Length, Decay, and Bell/Sustain should render/update the instrument silently; i/o/p and standalone Option/Alt trigger the selected grid entry.
- SF2 folder WAV export should operate on SF2 sample headers directly, saving one WAV per extracted mono sample or stereo pair as `SF2name-SF2Number-SampleName.wav`, without creating permanent Renoise instruments.

## decisions

- Velocity layers are GROUPS, not splits. Each group carries its own key range
  and its own velocity range (>Min/>Max); splits only subdivide a group by key.
  So Joshua's question "does the Voice format support velocity zones at the
  format level" is answered yes, and the implementation is N groups with
  overlapping key ranges and stacked velocity ranges.
- Trim exported waves at the loop end. The TX16W has no loop end, so not
  trimming makes the sampler play a longer loop than Renoise does. Lossless.
- Budget RAM against uncompressed frames, not file size. DWVW shrinks the disk
  copy only; the sampler holds the decoded audio.
- The 8-byte trailer on every Wave/Voic/Perf reference is a disk name. Writing
  the real volume label is what makes the sampler prompt for a named floppy.

-- SampleBrain/jobs/JobRunner.lua
-- Cooperative multitasking for heavy DSP operations in Renoise

local JobRunner = {}

local current_job = nil

local function idle_handler()
  if not current_job then
    if renoise and renoise.tool and renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:remove_notifier(idle_handler)
    end
    return
  end

  if current_job.cancelled then
    local finished_job = current_job
    current_job = nil
    if renoise and renoise.tool and renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:remove_notifier(idle_handler)
    end
    if finished_job.on_cancel then
      finished_job.on_cancel()
    end
    return
  end

  -- Record start time for time-budgeted yields
  current_job.last_yield_time = os.clock()

  local status, err = coroutine.resume(current_job.co, current_job)

  if coroutine.status(current_job.co) == "dead" then
    local finished_job = current_job
    current_job = nil
    if renoise and renoise.tool and renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:remove_notifier(idle_handler)
    end

    if status then
      if finished_job.on_complete then
        finished_job.on_complete(err)
      end
    else
      if finished_job.on_error then
        finished_job.on_error(err)
      else
        if renoise and renoise.app then
          renoise.app():show_error("SampleBrain Job Error:\n" .. tostring(err))
        else
          print("SampleBrain Job Error:\n" .. tostring(err))
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

--- Start a cooperative job
-- @param func function Coroutine body `function(job)`
-- @param on_progress function Callback for progress updates `function(percent, message)`
-- @param on_complete function Callback when finished `function(result)`
-- @param on_error function Callback on error `function(err)`
-- @param on_cancel function (Optional) Callback on cancellation `function()`
-- @return boolean true if started successfully
function JobRunner.start(func, on_progress, on_complete, on_error, on_cancel)
  if current_job then
    return false, "A job is already running."
  end

  current_job = {
    co = coroutine.create(func),
    on_progress = on_progress,
    on_complete = on_complete,
    on_error = on_error,
    on_cancel = on_cancel,
    cancelled = false,
    last_yield_time = os.clock()
  }

  if renoise and renoise.tool then
    if not renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:add_notifier(idle_handler)
    end
  else
    -- If no Renoise, run synchronously for tests
    while current_job do
      idle_handler()
    end
  end

  return true
end

--- Cancel the currently running job
function JobRunner.cancel()
  if current_job then
    current_job.cancelled = true
    -- We do NOT set current_job = nil here. 
    -- The next idle_handler execution will notice current_job.cancelled == true, 
    -- fire on_cancel(), and properly deregister the idle_handler.
  end
end

--- Check if a job is currently running
function JobRunner.is_running()
  return current_job ~= nil
end

--- Yield from within a job coroutine, optionally updating progress
-- Yielding happens only if forced or if the CPU time budget (e.g., 10ms) is exceeded.
-- @param job table The job instance passed to the coroutine
-- @param percent number 0.0 to 1.0 progress
-- @param message string Optional status message
-- @param force boolean If true, yield regardless of elapsed time
function JobRunner.yield(job, percent, message, force)
  if job.cancelled then
    coroutine.yield()
  end
  
  -- Use ~10ms CPU budget limit
  local elapsed = os.clock() - job.last_yield_time
  if force or elapsed > 0.010 then
    if job.on_progress and percent then
      job.on_progress(percent, message)
    end
    coroutine.yield()
    job.last_yield_time = os.clock() -- Reset timer after waking back up
  end
end

return JobRunner
-- SampleBrain/matching/Matcher.lua
-- Stateful search engine implementing Basic, Reversed, Synaptic, and Synaptic-Slide search algorithms

local Distance = require("SampleBrain.dsp.Distance")
local Constants = require("SampleBrain.Constants")

local Matcher = {}
Matcher.__index = Matcher

local function create_prng(seed)
  local state = (seed or 12345) % 2147483647
  if state <= 0 then state = state + 2147483646 end
  return function(min_val, max_val)
    state = (state * 16807) % 2147483647
    local frac = (state - 1) / 2147483646.0
    if min_val and max_val then
      return math.floor(min_val + frac * (max_val - min_val + 1))
    else
      return frac
    end
  end
end

function Matcher.create(brain_blocks)
  local m = setmetatable({
    brain_blocks = brain_blocks or {},
    current_block_index = 1,
    current_error = 0.0,
    usage_table = {},
    prng = create_prng(12345)
  }, Matcher)
  return m
end

function Matcher:reset(seed)
  self.prng = create_prng(seed or 12345)
  self.usage_table = {}
  if #self.brain_blocks > 0 then
    self.current_block_index = self.prng(1, #self.brain_blocks)
  else
    self.current_block_index = 1
  end
  self.current_error = 0.0
end

function Matcher:deplete_usage(falloff)
  falloff = falloff or Constants.USAGE_FALLOFF
  for idx, val in pairs(self.usage_table) do
    self.usage_table[idx] = val * falloff
  end
end

function Matcher:stickify(target_block, closest_index, dist, options)
  local stickiness = options.stickiness or Constants.DEFAULT_STICKINESS
  local mode = options.stickiness_mode or Constants.STICKINESS_UPSTREAM
  local next_index = self.current_block_index + 1

  if stickiness > 0 and next_index <= #self.brain_blocks then
    local next_blk = self.brain_blocks[next_index]
    
    local allow_stick = false
    if mode == Constants.STICKINESS_SAME_SOURCE then
      allow_stick = next_blk.source_ref.enabled and next_blk.source_ref.id == self.brain_blocks[self.current_block_index].source_ref.id
    else
      -- Upstream: just advance without checking source boundary, as long as it's enabled
      allow_stick = next_blk.source_ref.enabled
    end

    if allow_stick then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[next_index] or 0.0
      local dist_to_next = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, next_blk,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )

      if dist_to_next * (1.0 - stickiness) < dist * stickiness then
        self.current_block_index = next_index
        return self.current_block_index
      end
    end
  end

  self.current_block_index = closest_index
  return self.current_block_index
end

--- Basic Minimum Distance Search
function Matcher:search_basic(target_block, options)
  local min_dist = math.huge
  local closest_index = nil

  for i = 1, #self.brain_blocks do
    local b = self.brain_blocks[i]
    if b.source_ref.enabled then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[i] or 0.0
      local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, b,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )
      if dist < min_dist then
        min_dist = dist
        closest_index = i
      end
    end
  end

  if not closest_index then
    return nil, math.huge, "No enabled brain blocks"
  end

  self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
  self.usage_table[closest_index] = (self.usage_table[closest_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
  self.current_error = min_dist

  local chosen_idx = self:stickify(target_block, closest_index, min_dist, options)
  return self.brain_blocks[chosen_idx], min_dist
end

--- Reversed Maximum Distance Search
function Matcher:search_reversed(target_block, options)
  local max_dist = -1.0
  local furthest_index = nil

  for i = 1, #self.brain_blocks do
    local b = self.brain_blocks[i]
    if b.source_ref.enabled then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[i] or 0.0
      local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, b,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )
      if dist > max_dist then
        max_dist = dist
        furthest_index = i
      end
    end
  end

  if not furthest_index then
    return nil, math.huge, "No enabled brain blocks"
  end

  self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
  self.usage_table[furthest_index] = (self.usage_table[furthest_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
  self.current_error = max_dist
  self.current_block_index = furthest_index

  return self.brain_blocks[furthest_index], max_dist
end

--- Synaptic Graph Search
function Matcher:search_synaptic(target_block, options)
  local cur_block = self.brain_blocks[self.current_block_index]
  local channel = (options and options.channel) or "mono"
  local synapses = cur_block and cur_block.synapses
  if cur_block and channel == "left" and cur_block.synapses_l then
    synapses = cur_block.synapses_l
  elseif cur_block and channel == "right" and cur_block.synapses_r then
    synapses = cur_block.synapses_r
  end

  if not cur_block or not synapses or #synapses == 0 then
    -- Fallback to basic search if graph not initialized
    return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
  end

  local min_dist = math.huge
  local closest_index = nil
  local num_syn = math.min(#synapses, options.num_synapses or Constants.DEFAULT_NUM_SYNAPSES)

  for s = 1, num_syn do
    local syn_idx = synapses[s]
    local other_blk = self.brain_blocks[syn_idx]
    if other_blk and other_blk.source_ref.enabled then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[syn_idx] or 0.0
      local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, other_blk,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )
      if dist < min_dist then
        min_dist = dist
        closest_index = syn_idx
      end
    end
  end

  if not closest_index then
    local fallback_mode = options.fallback_mode or Constants.FALLBACK_HOLD_CURRENT
    if fallback_mode == Constants.FALLBACK_HOLD_CURRENT then
      -- Upstream: return current block immediately without calling stickify
      self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
      self.usage_table[self.current_block_index] = (self.usage_table[self.current_block_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
      self.current_error = math.huge
      return self.brain_blocks[self.current_block_index], math.huge
    else
      -- Fallback to global basic search across all active blocks
      return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
    end
  end

  local current_index = self.current_block_index

  self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
  self.usage_table[current_index] = (self.usage_table[current_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
  self.current_error = min_dist

  local chosen_idx = self:stickify(target_block, closest_index, min_dist, options)
  return self.brain_blocks[chosen_idx], min_dist
end

--- Choose block based on search algorithm
function Matcher:search(target_block, options)
  options = options or {}
  local algo = options.algo or Constants.ALGO_BASIC

  if algo == Constants.ALGO_BASIC then
    return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
  elseif algo == Constants.ALGO_REVERSED then
    return self:search_reversed(target_block, options)
  elseif algo == Constants.ALGO_SYNAPTIC or algo == Constants.ALGO_SYNAPTIC_SLIDE then
    return self:search_synaptic(target_block, options)
  else
    return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
  end
end

return Matcher
-- SampleBrain/matching/BasicMatcher.lua
-- Basic exhaustive search matcher (finds global minimum distance block)

local Distance = require("SampleBrain.dsp.Distance")
local Constants = require("SampleBrain.Constants")

local BasicMatcher = {}

--- Find closest brain block for a given target block
-- @param target_block table Target Block model
-- @param brain_blocks table Array of brain Block models
-- @param ratio number FFT vs MFCC ratio (0..1)
-- @param n_ratio number Raw vs Normalized ratio (0..1)
-- @param usage_importance number Usage/novelty penalty weight
-- @return table Best matching brain Block
-- @return number Minimum distance score
function BasicMatcher.match(target_block, brain_blocks, ratio, n_ratio, usage_importance)
  if #brain_blocks == 0 then return nil, math.huge end

  local min_dist = math.huge
  local best_block = nil

  for i = 1, #brain_blocks do
    local b = brain_blocks[i]
    local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(target_block, b, ratio, n_ratio, usage_importance)
    if dist < min_dist then
      min_dist = dist
      best_block = b
    end
  end

  return best_block, min_dist
end

return BasicMatcher

local MainDialog = require("SampleBrain.ui.MainDialog")

local Init = {}

end

if renoise and renoise.tool then
  renoise.tool().app_new_document_observable:add_notifier(function()
    MainDialog.reset_state()

-- Cooperative multitasking for heavy DSP operations in Renoise

local JobRunner = {}

local current_job = nil

local function idle_handler()
  if not current_job then
    if renoise and renoise.tool and renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:remove_notifier(idle_handler)
    end
    return
  end

  if current_job.cancelled then
    local finished_job = current_job
    current_job = nil
    if renoise and renoise.tool and renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:remove_notifier(idle_handler)
    end
    if finished_job.on_cancel then
      finished_job.on_cancel()
    end
    return
  end

  -- Record start time for time-budgeted yields
  current_job.last_yield_time = os.clock()

  local status, err = coroutine.resume(current_job.co, current_job)

  if coroutine.status(current_job.co) == "dead" then
    local finished_job = current_job
    current_job = nil
    if renoise and renoise.tool and renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:remove_notifier(idle_handler)
    end

    if status then
      if finished_job.on_complete then
        finished_job.on_complete(err)
      end
    else
      if finished_job.on_error then
        finished_job.on_error(err)
      else
        if renoise and renoise.app then
          renoise.app():show_error("SampleBrain Job Error:\n" .. tostring(err))
        else
          print("SampleBrain Job Error:\n" .. tostring(err))
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

--- Start a cooperative job
-- @param func function Coroutine body `function(job)`
-- @param on_progress function Callback for progress updates `function(percent, message)`
-- @param on_complete function Callback when finished `function(result)`
-- @param on_error function Callback on error `function(err)`
-- @param on_cancel function (Optional) Callback on cancellation `function()`
-- @return boolean true if started successfully
function JobRunner.start(func, on_progress, on_complete, on_error, on_cancel)
  if current_job then
    return false, "A job is already running."
  end

  current_job = {
    co = coroutine.create(func),
    on_progress = on_progress,
    on_complete = on_complete,
    on_error = on_error,
    on_cancel = on_cancel,
    cancelled = false,
    last_yield_time = os.clock()
  }

  if renoise and renoise.tool then
    if not renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:has_notifier(idle_handler) then
      renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:add_notifier(idle_handler)
    end
  else
    -- If no Renoise, run synchronously for tests
    while current_job do
      idle_handler()
    end
  end

  return true
end

--- Cancel the currently running job
function JobRunner.cancel()
  if current_job then
    current_job.cancelled = true
    -- We do NOT set current_job = nil here. 
    -- The next idle_handler execution will notice current_job.cancelled == true, 
    -- fire on_cancel(), and properly deregister the idle_handler.
  end
end

--- Check if a job is currently running
function JobRunner.is_running()
  return current_job ~= nil
end

--- Yield from within a job coroutine, optionally updating progress
-- Yielding happens only if forced or if the CPU time budget (e.g., 10ms) is exceeded.
-- @param job table The job instance passed to the coroutine
-- @param percent number 0.0 to 1.0 progress
-- @param message string Optional status message
-- @param force boolean If true, yield regardless of elapsed time
function JobRunner.yield(job, percent, message, force)
  if job.cancelled then
    coroutine.yield()
  end
  
  -- Use ~10ms CPU budget limit
  local elapsed = os.clock() - job.last_yield_time
  if force or elapsed > 0.010 then
    if job.on_progress and percent then
      job.on_progress(percent, message)
    end
    coroutine.yield()
    job.last_yield_time = os.clock() -- Reset timer after waking back up
  end
end

return JobRunner

-- Stateful search engine implementing Basic, Reversed, Synaptic, and Synaptic-Slide search algorithms

local Distance = require("SampleBrain.dsp.Distance")
local Constants = require("SampleBrain.Constants")

local Matcher = {}
Matcher.__index = Matcher

local function create_prng(seed)
  local state = (seed or 12345) % 2147483647
  if state <= 0 then state = state + 2147483646 end
  return function(min_val, max_val)
    state = (state * 16807) % 2147483647
    local frac = (state - 1) / 2147483646.0
    if min_val and max_val then
      return math.floor(min_val + frac * (max_val - min_val + 1))
    else
      return frac
    end
  end
end

function Matcher.create(brain_blocks)
  local m = setmetatable({
    brain_blocks = brain_blocks or {},
    current_block_index = 1,
    current_error = 0.0,
    usage_table = {},
    prng = create_prng(12345)
  }, Matcher)
  return m
end

function Matcher:reset(seed)
  self.prng = create_prng(seed or 12345)
  self.usage_table = {}
  if #self.brain_blocks > 0 then
    self.current_block_index = self.prng(1, #self.brain_blocks)
  else
    self.current_block_index = 1
  end
  self.current_error = 0.0
end

function Matcher:deplete_usage(falloff)
  falloff = falloff or Constants.USAGE_FALLOFF
  for idx, val in pairs(self.usage_table) do
    self.usage_table[idx] = val * falloff
  end
end

function Matcher:stickify(target_block, closest_index, dist, options)
  local stickiness = options.stickiness or Constants.DEFAULT_STICKINESS
  local mode = options.stickiness_mode or Constants.STICKINESS_UPSTREAM
  local next_index = self.current_block_index + 1

  if stickiness > 0 and next_index <= #self.brain_blocks then
    local next_blk = self.brain_blocks[next_index]
    
    local allow_stick = false
    if mode == Constants.STICKINESS_SAME_SOURCE then
      allow_stick = next_blk.source_ref.enabled and next_blk.source_ref.id == self.brain_blocks[self.current_block_index].source_ref.id
    else
      -- Upstream: just advance without checking source boundary, as long as it's enabled
      allow_stick = next_blk.source_ref.enabled
    end

    if allow_stick then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[next_index] or 0.0
      local dist_to_next = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, next_blk,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )

      if dist_to_next * (1.0 - stickiness) < dist * stickiness then
        self.current_block_index = next_index
        return self.current_block_index
      end
    end
  end

  self.current_block_index = closest_index
  return self.current_block_index
end

--- Basic Minimum Distance Search
function Matcher:search_basic(target_block, options)
  local min_dist = math.huge
  local closest_index = nil

  for i = 1, #self.brain_blocks do
    local b = self.brain_blocks[i]
    if b.source_ref.enabled then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[i] or 0.0
      local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, b,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )
      if dist < min_dist then
        min_dist = dist
        closest_index = i
      end
    end
  end

  if not closest_index then
    return nil, math.huge, "No enabled brain blocks"
  end

  self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
  self.usage_table[closest_index] = (self.usage_table[closest_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
  self.current_error = min_dist

  local chosen_idx = self:stickify(target_block, closest_index, min_dist, options)
  return self.brain_blocks[chosen_idx], min_dist
end

--- Reversed Maximum Distance Search
function Matcher:search_reversed(target_block, options)
  local max_dist = -1.0
  local furthest_index = nil

  for i = 1, #self.brain_blocks do
    local b = self.brain_blocks[i]
    if b.source_ref.enabled then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[i] or 0.0
      local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, b,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )
      if dist > max_dist then
        max_dist = dist
        furthest_index = i
      end
    end
  end

  if not furthest_index then
    return nil, math.huge, "No enabled brain blocks"
  end

  self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
  self.usage_table[furthest_index] = (self.usage_table[furthest_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
  self.current_error = max_dist
  self.current_block_index = furthest_index

  return self.brain_blocks[furthest_index], max_dist
end

--- Synaptic Graph Search
function Matcher:search_synaptic(target_block, options)
  local cur_block = self.brain_blocks[self.current_block_index]
  local channel = (options and options.channel) or "mono"
  local synapses = cur_block and cur_block.synapses
  if cur_block and channel == "left" and cur_block.synapses_l then
    synapses = cur_block.synapses_l
  elseif cur_block and channel == "right" and cur_block.synapses_r then
    synapses = cur_block.synapses_r
  end

  if not cur_block or not synapses or #synapses == 0 then
    -- Fallback to basic search if graph not initialized
    return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
  end

  local min_dist = math.huge
  local closest_index = nil
  local num_syn = math.min(#synapses, options.num_synapses or Constants.DEFAULT_NUM_SYNAPSES)

  for s = 1, num_syn do
    local syn_idx = synapses[s]
    local other_blk = self.brain_blocks[syn_idx]
    if other_blk and other_blk.source_ref.enabled then
      local candidate_usage = self.usage_table[syn_idx] or 0.0
      local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(
        target_block, other_blk,
        options.ratio, options.n_ratio, options.usage_importance,
        options.fft_start, options.fft_end, options.channel, candidate_usage
      )
      if dist < min_dist then
        min_dist = dist
        closest_index = syn_idx
      end
    end
  end

  if not closest_index then
    local fallback_mode = options.fallback_mode or Constants.FALLBACK_HOLD_CURRENT
    if fallback_mode == Constants.FALLBACK_HOLD_CURRENT then
      -- Upstream: return current block immediately without calling stickify
      self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
      self.usage_table[self.current_block_index] = (self.usage_table[self.current_block_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
      self.current_error = math.huge
      return self.brain_blocks[self.current_block_index], math.huge
    else
      -- Fallback to global basic search across all active blocks
      return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
    end
  end

  local current_index = self.current_block_index

  self:deplete_usage(options.usage_falloff)
  self.usage_table[current_index] = (self.usage_table[current_index] or 0.0) + Constants.USAGE_FACTOR
  self.current_error = min_dist

  local chosen_idx = self:stickify(target_block, closest_index, min_dist, options)
  return self.brain_blocks[chosen_idx], min_dist
end

--- Choose block based on search algorithm
function Matcher:search(target_block, options)
  options = options or {}
  local algo = options.algo or Constants.ALGO_BASIC

  if algo == Constants.ALGO_BASIC then
    return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
  elseif algo == Constants.ALGO_REVERSED then
    return self:search_reversed(target_block, options)
  elseif algo == Constants.ALGO_SYNAPTIC or algo == Constants.ALGO_SYNAPTIC_SLIDE then
    return self:search_synaptic(target_block, options)
  else
    return self:search_basic(target_block, options)
  end
end

return Matcher

-- Basic exhaustive search matcher (finds global minimum distance block)

local Distance = require("SampleBrain.dsp.Distance")
local Constants = require("SampleBrain.Constants")

local BasicMatcher = {}

--- Find closest brain block for a given target block
-- @param target_block table Target Block model
-- @param brain_blocks table Array of brain Block models
-- @param ratio number FFT vs MFCC ratio (0..1)
-- @param n_ratio number Raw vs Normalized ratio (0..1)
-- @param usage_importance number Usage/novelty penalty weight
-- @return table Best matching brain Block
-- @return number Minimum distance score
function BasicMatcher.match(target_block, brain_blocks, ratio, n_ratio, usage_importance)
  if #brain_blocks == 0 then return nil, math.huge end

  local min_dist = math.huge
  local best_block = nil

  for i = 1, #brain_blocks do
    local b = brain_blocks[i]
    local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(target_block, b, ratio, n_ratio, usage_importance)
    if dist < min_dist then
      min_dist = dist
      best_block = b
    end
  end

  return best_block, min_dist
end

return BasicMatcher

-- Concatenative synthesis renderer matching C++ SampleBrain renderer.cpp

local Matcher = require("SampleBrain.matching.Matcher")
local OverlapAdd = require("SampleBrain.render.OverlapAdd")
local Constants = require("SampleBrain.Constants")
local JobRunner = require("SampleBrain.jobs.JobRunner")

local Renderer = {}

--- Resample grain PCM array by pitch_scale ratio (linear interpolation)
-- @param pcm table Original PCM array
-- @param scale number Pitch ratio (1.0 = normal speed)
-- @return table Resampled PCM array
local function resample_grain(pcm, scale)
  if math.abs(scale - 1.0) < 1e-4 or scale <= 0 then
    return pcm
  end

  local src_len = #pcm
  local dst_len = math.max(1, math.floor(src_len / scale))
  local out = {}

  for i = 1, dst_len do
    local src_pos = (i - 1) * scale + 1
    local idx0 = math.floor(src_pos)
    local idx1 = math.min(src_len, idx0 + 1)
    local frac = src_pos - idx0

    if idx0 >= src_len then
      out[i] = pcm[src_len] or 0.0
    else
      local s0 = pcm[idx0] or 0.0
      local s1 = pcm[idx1] or 0.0
      out[i] = s0 * (1.0 - frac) + s1 * frac
    end
  end

  return out
end

-- @param brain_blocks table Array of brain Block instances
-- @param target_blocks table Array of target Block instances

-- Builds synaptic similarity graph across brain blocks

local Distance = require("SampleBrain.dsp.Distance")
local Constants = require("SampleBrain.Constants")
local JobRunner = require("SampleBrain.jobs.JobRunner")

local SynapseBuilder = {}

--- Build fixed nearest-neighbor synaptic graph for brain blocks (up to 1000 synapses)
-- @param brain_blocks table Array of Block instances
-- @param max_synapses integer Maximum synapses per block to store (default 1000)
-- @param ratio number FFT/MFCC mix ratio
-- @param n_ratio number Raw/Norm mix ratio
-- @param fft_start integer Optional FFT start bin
-- @param fft_end integer Optional FFT end bin
-- @param job table Optional job object for yielding
-- @return integer Total synapses created
function SynapseBuilder.build_fixed(brain_blocks, max_synapses, ratio, n_ratio, fft_start, fft_end, job, channel)
  max_synapses = math.min(max_synapses or 1000, 1000)
  ratio = ratio or Constants.DEFAULT_RATIO
  n_ratio = n_ratio or Constants.DEFAULT_N_RATIO

  local total_blocks = #brain_blocks
  if total_blocks == 0 then return 0 end

  local num_to_store_limit = math.min(max_synapses, total_blocks - 1)
  local total_synapses_created = 0

  local temp_graph = {}

  for i = 1, total_blocks do
    local block_a = brain_blocks[i]
    local candidates = {}

    for j = 1, total_blocks do
      if i ~= j then
        local block_b = brain_blocks[j]
        local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(block_a, block_b, ratio, n_ratio, 0.0, fft_start, fft_end, channel)
        candidates[#candidates + 1] = { index = j, distance = dist }
      end
      if job and (j % 20 == 0) then
        local total_comps = total_blocks * total_blocks
        local current_comp = (i - 1) * total_blocks + j
        JobRunner.yield(job, current_comp / total_comps, string.format("Building synapses %d%%", math.floor(current_comp / total_comps * 100)), false)
      end
    end

    table.sort(candidates, function(a, b) return a.distance < b.distance end)

    local block_synapses = {}
    local num_to_store = math.min(num_to_store_limit, #candidates)
    for n = 1, num_to_store do
      block_synapses[n] = candidates[n].index
    end
    temp_graph[i] = block_synapses

    total_synapses_created = total_synapses_created + #block_synapses

    if job then
      JobRunner.yield(job, i / total_blocks, string.format("Building synapses %d%%", math.floor(i / total_blocks * 100)), false)
    end
  end

  -- Atomic commit to live blocks
  for i = 1, total_blocks do
    if channel == "left" then
      brain_blocks[i].synapses_l = temp_graph[i]
    elseif channel == "right" then
      brain_blocks[i].synapses_r = temp_graph[i]
    else
      brain_blocks[i].synapses = temp_graph[i]
    end
  end

  return total_synapses_created
end

return SynapseBuilder

--- Resample grain PCM array by pitch_scale ratio (linear interpolation)
-- @param pcm table Original PCM array
-- @param scale number Pitch ratio (1.0 = normal speed)
-- @return table Resampled PCM array
local function resample_grain(pcm, scale)
  if math.abs(scale - 1.0) < 1e-4 or scale <= 0 then
    return pcm
  end

  local src_len = #pcm
  local dst_len = math.max(1, math.floor(src_len / scale))
  local out = {}

  for i = 1, dst_len do
    local src_pos = (i - 1) * scale + 1
    local idx0 = math.floor(src_pos)
    local idx1 = math.min(src_len, idx0 + 1)
    local frac = src_pos - idx0

    if idx0 >= src_len then
      out[i] = pcm[src_len] or 0.0
    else
      local s0 = pcm[idx0] or 0.0
      local s1 = pcm[idx1] or 0.0
      out[i] = s0 * (1.0 - frac) + s1 * frac
    end
  end

  return out
end

--- Render concatenative output from brain and target blocks
-- @param brain_blocks table Array of brain Block instances
-- @param target_blocks table Array of target Block instances
-- @param options table Render options table
-- @return table Output float PCM array
function Renderer.render(brain_blocks, target_blocks, options)
  options = options or {}
  local block_size = options.block_size or Constants.DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE
  local overlap = options.overlap or Constants.DEFAULT_OVERLAP
  local window_type = options.window_type or Constants.WINDOW_HANN
  local ratio = options.ratio or Constants.DEFAULT_RATIO
  local n_ratio = options.n_ratio or Constants.DEFAULT_N_RATIO
  local usage_importance = options.usage_importance or Constants.DEFAULT_USAGE_IMPORTANCE
  local usage_falloff = options.usage_falloff or Constants.USAGE_FALLOFF
  local stickiness = options.stickiness or Constants.DEFAULT_STICKINESS
  local fft_start = options.fft_start or 1
  local fft_end = options.fft_end or Constants.FFT_BINS_CROPPED
  local algo = options.algo or Constants.ALGO_BASIC
  local stretch = options.stretch or 1
  local autotune = options.autotune or 0.0
  local n_mix = options.n_mix or 0.0
  local target_mix = options.target_mix or 0.0
  local brain_gain = options.brain_gain or 1.0
  local slide_error = options.slide_error or Constants.DEFAULT_SLIDE_ERROR

  local independent_stereo = options.independent_stereo or false
  local matcher_l = Matcher.create(brain_blocks)
  local matcher_r = independent_stereo and Matcher.create(brain_blocks) or matcher_l
  matcher_l:reset(options.seed)
  if independent_stereo then matcher_r:reset((options.seed or 12345) + 1) end

  local target_rate = (target_blocks[1] and target_blocks[1].sample_rate) or Constants.DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE
  local canonical_hop = math.max(1, math.floor(block_size * (1.0 - overlap)))
  local exact_output_hop = canonical_hop * target_rate / Constants.DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE
  local decisions = {}

  local target_idx = 1
  local render_step = 0

  local slide_attempts = 0
  local max_slide_attempts = options.max_slide_attempts or 100

  -- Phase 1: Search & Decision Stream Generation
  while target_idx <= #target_blocks do
    local target_blk = target_blocks[target_idx]
    local search_opts_l = {
      algo = algo,
      ratio = ratio,
      n_ratio = n_ratio,
      usage_importance = usage_importance,
      usage_falloff = usage_falloff,
      stickiness = stickiness,
      fft_start = fft_start,
      fft_end = fft_end,
      num_synapses = options.num_synapses,
      channel = "left"
    }

    local matched_blk_l, dist_l, err_l = matcher_l:search(target_blk, search_opts_l)
    if not matched_blk_l then
      return nil, err_l or "Left matcher returned no block"
    end

    local matched_blk_r = matched_blk_l
    local dist_r = dist_l
    if independent_stereo then
      local search_opts_r = {
        algo = algo,
        ratio = ratio,
        n_ratio = n_ratio,
        usage_importance = usage_importance,
        usage_falloff = usage_falloff,
        stickiness = stickiness,
        fft_start = fft_start,
        fft_end = fft_end,
        num_synapses = options.num_synapses,
        channel = "right"
      }
      local m_r, d_r, e_r = matcher_r:search(target_blk, search_opts_r)
      if not m_r then
        return nil, e_r or "Right matcher returned no block"
      end
      matched_blk_r = m_r
      dist_r = d_r
    end

    decisions[#decisions + 1] = {
      target_blk = target_blk,
      matched_blk = matched_blk_l,
      matched_blk_l = matched_blk_l,
      matched_blk_r = matched_blk_r,
      render_step = render_step,
      dist = dist_l
    }

    -- Target step logic (incorporating Synaptic Slide & Stretch)
    if algo == Constants.ALGO_SYNAPTIC_SLIDE then
      if slide_attempts >= max_slide_attempts then
        -- Force target advance if slide_error threshold cannot be satisfied within repeat limit
        target_idx = target_idx + 1
        slide_attempts = 0
      elseif matcher_l.current_error < slide_error and (render_step % stretch == 0) then
        target_idx = target_idx + 1
        slide_attempts = 0
      else
        slide_attempts = slide_attempts + 1
      end
    else
      if render_step % stretch == 0 then
        target_idx = target_idx + 1
      end
    end

    render_step = render_step + 1

    if options.job then
      JobRunner.yield(options.job, target_idx / #target_blocks, string.format("Matching block %d / %d", target_idx, #target_blocks), false)
    end
  end

  -- Phase 2: Overlap-Add Rendering from Decision Stream
  local total_output_frames = math.max(1, math.ceil((render_step - 1) * exact_output_hop + block_size))
  local ola_l = OverlapAdd.create(total_output_frames)
  local ola_r = OverlapAdd.create(total_output_frames)

  for idx = 1, #decisions do
    local dec = decisions[idx]
    local target_blk = dec.target_blk
    local matched_l = dec.matched_blk_l or dec.matched_blk
    local matched_r = dec.matched_blk_r or dec.matched_blk

    local raw_l, _ = matched_l:get_windowed_pcm_stereo()
    local _, raw_r = matched_r:get_windowed_pcm_stereo()
    local n_raw_l, _ = matched_l:get_normalized_windowed_pcm_stereo()
    local _, n_raw_r = matched_r:get_normalized_windowed_pcm_stereo()
    local targ_l, targ_r = target_blk:get_windowed_pcm_stereo()

    local target_len = #targ_l
    local grain_l = {}
    local grain_r = {}

    local src_len_l = math.max(#raw_l, #n_raw_l)
    local src_len_r = math.max(#raw_r, #n_raw_r)
    local comp_gain = brain_gain * (options.normalize and 1.0 or 0.2)

    -- Sample-rate compensation scale for Left and Right channels
    local dst_rate = target_blk.sample_rate or Constants.DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE
    local src_rate_l = matched_l.sample_rate or Constants.DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE
    local src_rate_r = matched_r.sample_rate or Constants.DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE

    -- Independent pitch scales
    local pitch_scale_l = 1.0
    local pitch_scale_r = 1.0

    if autotune > 0 then
      local dom_target_l = target_blk.dominant_freq_l or target_blk.dominant_freq
      local dom_target_r = target_blk.dominant_freq_r or target_blk.dominant_freq
      local dom_match_l = matched_l.dominant_freq_l or matched_l.dominant_freq
      local dom_match_r = matched_r.dominant_freq_r or matched_r.dominant_freq

      if dom_target_l and dom_match_l and dom_match_l > 0 then
        pitch_scale_l = dom_target_l / dom_match_l
        local max_scale = 1.0 + (autotune * autotune) * 100.0
        if pitch_scale_l > max_scale then pitch_scale_l = max_scale end
        if pitch_scale_l < 1.0 / max_scale then pitch_scale_l = 1.0 / max_scale end
      end

      if dom_target_r and dom_match_r and dom_match_r > 0 then
        pitch_scale_r = dom_target_r / dom_match_r
        local max_scale = 1.0 + (autotune * autotune) * 100.0
        if pitch_scale_r > max_scale then pitch_scale_r = max_scale end
        if pitch_scale_r < 1.0 / max_scale then pitch_scale_r = 1.0 / max_scale end
      end
    end

    local cursor_step_l = pitch_scale_l * ((src_rate_l > 0 and dst_rate > 0) and (src_rate_l / dst_rate) or 1.0)
    local cursor_step_r = pitch_scale_r * ((src_rate_r > 0 and dst_rate > 0) and (src_rate_r / dst_rate) or 1.0)

    -- Upstream Source Cursor Rendering Semantics (Independent L/R Cursors)
    local source_position_l = 0.0
    local source_position_r = 0.0
    local block_pos = 0

    while (source_position_l < src_len_l or source_position_r < src_len_r) do
      local idx0_l = math.floor(source_position_l)
      local idx0_r = math.floor(source_position_r)
      local r_s_l, r_s_r, n_s_l, n_s_r

      if idx0_l >= src_len_l - 1 then
        r_s_l = raw_l[src_len_l] or 0.0
        n_s_l = n_raw_l[src_len_l] or 0.0
      else
        local frac = source_position_l - idx0_l
        r_s_l = (raw_l[idx0_l + 1] or 0.0) * (1.0 - frac) + (raw_l[idx0_l + 2] or 0.0) * frac
        n_s_l = (n_raw_l[idx0_l + 1] or 0.0) * (1.0 - frac) + (n_raw_l[idx0_l + 2] or 0.0) * frac
      end

      if idx0_r >= src_len_r - 1 then
        r_s_r = raw_r[src_len_r] or 0.0
        n_s_r = n_raw_r[src_len_r] or 0.0
      else
        local frac = source_position_r - idx0_r
        r_s_r = (raw_r[idx0_r + 1] or 0.0) * (1.0 - frac) + (raw_r[idx0_r + 2] or 0.0) * frac
        n_s_r = (n_raw_r[idx0_r + 1] or 0.0) * (1.0 - frac) + (n_raw_r[idx0_r + 2] or 0.0) * frac
      end

      local brain_sample_l = r_s_l * (1.0 - n_mix) + n_s_l * n_mix
      local brain_sample_r = r_s_r * (1.0 - n_mix) + n_s_r * n_mix

      local t_s_l = 0.0
      local t_s_r = 0.0

      if block_pos < target_len then
        t_s_l = targ_l[block_pos + 1] or 0.0
        t_s_r = targ_r[block_pos + 1] or 0.0
      end

      grain_l[block_pos + 1] = brain_sample_l * (1.0 - target_mix) + t_s_l * target_mix
      grain_r[block_pos + 1] = brain_sample_r * (1.0 - target_mix) + t_s_r * target_mix

      source_position_l = source_position_l + cursor_step_l
      source_position_r = source_position_r + cursor_step_r

      if block_pos < src_len_l and source_position_l > src_len_l then
        source_position_l = 0.0
      end
      if block_pos < src_len_r and source_position_r > src_len_r then
        source_position_r = 0.0
      end

      block_pos = block_pos + 1

      -- Dynamic rate-aware watchdog cap (accounting for both L and R lifespans)
      local max_len_l = math.max(src_len_l, math.ceil(src_len_l / math.max(cursor_step_l, 1e-6)))
      local max_len_r = math.max(src_len_r, math.ceil(src_len_r / math.max(cursor_step_r, 1e-6)))
      local watchdog_cap = (math.max(max_len_l, max_len_r) + target_len) * 5
      if block_pos > watchdog_cap then
        break
      end
    end

    -- Update total bounds based on actual rendered grain tails
    local start_frame = math.floor(dec.render_step * exact_output_hop + 0.5) + 1
    local end_frame = start_frame + #grain_l - 1
    if end_frame > total_output_frames then
      total_output_frames = end_frame
      ola_l:resize(total_output_frames)
      ola_r:resize(total_output_frames)
    end

    ola_l:add_grain(grain_l, start_frame, comp_gain, Constants.WINDOW_RECTANGLE)
    ola_r:add_grain(grain_r, start_frame, comp_gain, Constants.WINDOW_RECTANGLE)

    if options.job then
      JobRunner.yield(options.job, idx / #decisions, string.format("Rendering audio %d / %d", idx, #decisions), false)
    end
  end

  if options.normalize then
    -- Shared peak normalization to preserve stereo balance
    local max_l = 0.0
    for i = 1, ola_l.length do local v = math.abs(ola_l.buffer[i]); if v > max_l then max_l = v end end
    local max_r = 0.0
    for i = 1, ola_r.length do local v = math.abs(ola_r.buffer[i]); if v > max_r then max_r = v end end
    local shared_peak = math.max(max_l, max_r)
    if shared_peak > 1e-12 then
      local scale = 0.98 / shared_peak
      for i = 1, ola_l.length do ola_l.buffer[i] = ola_l.buffer[i] * scale end
      for i = 1, ola_r.length do ola_r.buffer[i] = ola_r.buffer[i] * scale end
    end
  end

  return ola_l.buffer, ola_r.buffer
end

return Renderer

-- SampleBrain/analysis/SynapseBuilder.lua
-- Builds synaptic similarity graph across brain blocks

local Distance = require("SampleBrain.dsp.Distance")
local Constants = require("SampleBrain.Constants")
local JobRunner = require("SampleBrain.jobs.JobRunner")

local SynapseBuilder = {}

--- Build fixed nearest-neighbor synaptic graph for brain blocks (up to 1000 synapses)
-- @param brain_blocks table Array of Block instances
-- @param max_synapses integer Maximum synapses per block to store (default 1000)
-- @param ratio number FFT/MFCC mix ratio
-- @param n_ratio number Raw/Norm mix ratio
-- @param fft_start integer Optional FFT start bin
-- @param fft_end integer Optional FFT end bin
-- @param job table Optional job object for yielding
-- @return integer Total synapses created
function SynapseBuilder.build_fixed(brain_blocks, max_synapses, ratio, n_ratio, fft_start, fft_end, job, channel)
  max_synapses = math.min(max_synapses or 1000, 1000)
  ratio = ratio or Constants.DEFAULT_RATIO
  n_ratio = n_ratio or Constants.DEFAULT_N_RATIO

  local total_blocks = #brain_blocks
  if total_blocks == 0 then return 0 end

  local num_to_store_limit = math.min(max_synapses, total_blocks - 1)
  local total_synapses_created = 0

  local temp_graph = {}

  for i = 1, total_blocks do
    local block_a = brain_blocks[i]
    local candidates = {}

    for j = 1, total_blocks do
      if i ~= j then
        local block_b = brain_blocks[j]
        local dist = Distance.compare_blocks(block_a, block_b, ratio, n_ratio, 0.0, fft_start, fft_end, channel)
        candidates[#candidates + 1] = { index = j, distance = dist }
      end
      if job and (j % 20 == 0) then
        local total_comps = total_blocks * total_blocks
        local current_comp = (i - 1) * total_blocks + j
        JobRunner.yield(job, current_comp / total_comps, string.format("Building synapses %d%%", math.floor(current_comp / total_comps * 100)), false)
      end
    end

    table.sort(candidates, function(a, b) return a.distance < b.distance end)

    local block_synapses = {}
    local num_to_store = math.min(num_to_store_limit, #candidates)
    for n = 1, num_to_store do
      block_synapses[n] = candidates[n].index
    end
    temp_graph[i] = block_synapses

    total_synapses_created = total_synapses_created + #block_synapses

    if job then
      JobRunner.yield(job, i / total_blocks, string.format("Building synapses %d%%", math.floor(i / total_blocks * 100)), false)
    end
  end

  -- Atomic commit to live blocks
  for i = 1, total_blocks do
    if channel == "left" then
      brain_blocks[i].synapses_l = temp_graph[i]
    elseif channel == "right" then
      brain_blocks[i].synapses_r = temp_graph[i]
    else
      brain_blocks[i].synapses = temp_graph[i]
    end
  end

  return total_synapses_created
end

return SynapseBuilder
